episodes.197826: From January 6th through January 10th, a strong South Pacific Convergence Zone (SPCZ) strengthened over the American Samoa islands. WSO Pago Pago recorded 16.33 inches of rain during these 5 days and 21.39 inches of rainfall was measured from Jan 04th through the 10th. This is the highest seven day rainfall event recorded at the WSO Pago Pago office. Sustained winds reached over 40 MPH with gusts over 50 MPH at times, which was recorded by the WSO Pago Pago station and the NOAA observatory in Tula.  Impacts from the SPCZ's strong winds and heavy rainfall include: landslides, numerous trees knocked over, widespread flash flooding, airline cancelations for all islands, American Samoa's Governor closing all schools on January 10th, and multiple island wide power outages for Tutuila island. Two daily rainfall records were broken (January 9th and 10th).
episodes.198963: A mesoscale convective complex formed within an upper level trough axis centered over the eastern half of the state. Severe thunderstorms developed east of this trough axis and moved south onto the island of Maui.

A parked plane was blown into another parked plane. The nose of one plane pierced the bottom of a plane parked perpendicular to it. Damage cost was estimated.

Local police and a WSO Pago Pago employee reported flash flooding occurred along Fagaima Road on the morning of the 10th. At least 6 inches of water was flowing from the TMO intersection to the Georgina Building. Significant ponding of at least 3 feet occurred near the Georgina building. Water was seen flowing into multiple residential buildings in the area. Rainfall estimated to be around 5 inches between 8 AM and 12 PM with and estimated 8 inches of total rainfall on the 10th.

American Samoa Emergency Management office reports flash flooding occurred near the correctional facility in Tafuna on the morning of the 10th. Significant water from the Taumata and Vaitele streams overflowed the region's ditch systems onto the road at Lions Park. Pictures show around 6 inches of water moved over the roadway as the water moved into the Pala Lagoon as well as significant ponding over the area. Damage to the correctional facility and park is unknown.

Local media and numerous facebook posts reported heavy rainfall along the villages of Laulii and Aumi on the morning of January 10th. This led to a considerable amount of rainwater to flow down Pioa mountain to move through the villages and into Laulii Bay. Residents complained of red sediment and water moving into multiple residential buildings during this time. Videos showed over 6 inches of water flowing through streets of the villages along with flooded houses.

Pictures from a Facebook post show the Maloata Bridge flooded due to rainfall flowing off of Lealafaalava mountain. At least 6 inches of water was seen flowing onto the bridge and overflowing into the Maloata stream.

American Samoa EOC (Emergency Operations Center) reported a flooded home in the village of Alao due to the overflowing Vaimumu stream. Water covered the residential floor. An estimated 5.5 inches fell in the region between 8 AM and 12 PM.

Assistance was requested for Red Cross due to a flooded home in the village of Nuuuli on the morning of the 10th. Due to storm water drainage issues at Nuuuli (Coconut Point), flash flooding overflowed the drainage system. This water flowed onto driveway and inside home.
